description:
The dated sequence of what has been observed for one domain, oldest first: when a zone file first listed it, certificates issued, when addresses were first observed, and DNS answer changes. NEEDS AN API KEY ON THE PLUS PLAN OR ABOVE.

Use it when the ORDER and the gaps matter (registration to first certificate, certificate to first answer). Every event names its source and its precision (exact, day or observed), and gap_seconds is the time since the previous event. An event is when WE observed it, which bounds when it happened; it is not a registry's own timestamp. For the current state use lookup_domain (free) or domain_detail instead.

One reply holds up to 2000 events, with no paging. Certificate events come only from the live certificate table, the last 32 hours (cert_window_days in the reply), so older issuance is not listed here; lookup_domain's first_cert_seen gives the first one. A domain with nothing observed returns a not-found result, which means nothing held, not an inactive domain.

domain.description: The registrable domain, e.g. "example.co.uk". A URL or a leading www. is accepted and stripped; other subdomains are not folded, so pass "example.co.uk", not "mail.example.co.uk".
